wata-mac grows without bound while IDLE — macOS paused it at 26 GB after days of running (owner, 2026-08-08). MEASURED AND REPRODUCIBLE, root cause NOT found. `just mac-leak` drives pure idle frames and samples three numbers together so the answer says WHERE: RSS +4-5 MB per ~40s (~400 MB/hour, which is ~60h to 26 GB and matches the uptime), Go LIVE HEAP FLAT at 1-2 MB across the run, and OS THREADS 6->13 monotonic. RULED OUT so far: Go objects (flat live heap over the same window) and retained ObjC objects (two `heap <pid>` censuses 60 rounds apart are class-for-class IDENTICAL — capture with `heap` before and after and diff the COUNT/BYTES table under the `CLASS_NAME` header). The only signal moving with RSS is the thread count, which points at goroutines that never finish, each pinning an M, rather than at any heap. NEXT PROBES, in order: (1) SIGQUIT the app mid-run for a goroutine dump — it names the leaking goroutine and its creation site directly, and is the cheapest decisive step; (2) `vmmap <pid>` before/after to see which region grows, which separates thread stacks from a malloc zone. CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE FORGOTTEN: mac-leak runs HEADLESS, where nothing drives an NSApplication runloop, so main-queue work is never drained and nativeui/dispatch.go's `pending` map grows — a growth source the WINDOWED app does not have. The owner's 26 GB was the windowed app, so a candidate found here is a lead and any fix must be confirmed against a real windowed run

title: the `-page_duration 20000` flag in tools/make-chirp.py is now INERT and should go at the next regeneration. It existed because the old reader took a page's payload as one frame, so an ffmpeg-default chirp read as a single oversized frame; Ogg.readFrames walks the lacing table now and the asset would be correct without it. It cannot simply be deleted: the asset is committed as BYTES and `--check` has to keep reproducing them, so the flag comes out only when the chirp is next re-encoded from the owner's source recording (which lives on the owner's machine only). Nothing breaks meanwhile — this is a tidy-up whose trigger is someone else's file

the HANDSET half of the arrival notification. The MODEL IS SETTLED and shared: `wataclient/src/main/scala/notify.scala` owns NotifyMode (NotifyPlayNow/NotifyQuiet), Arrival, and Notify.step — the arrival edge is a conversation's unplayed count rising, priming is once per SESSION (a DM room is created by its first message, so per-conversation priming silences the arrival most worth having), and the mac's decisions are pinned by `wata-fb notifytest` in ci plus `just mac-notify-smoke`. What is left is wata-fb's presentation of the same two modes: PLAY IMMEDIATELY walkie-talkie style — except when the volume knob is off, which is also the screen-off/silent position — and a quiet mode that blinks the LED, shows an in-app banner and HIGHLIGHTS the conversation rather than only bumping a count, which a kid is unlikely to notice. title: the red recording bar should carry a mini spectrum-analyzer / level animation driven by the LIVE capture level, so holding PTT visibly proves the mic is working. Motivated by 2026-08-07: `DEC1 MUX` reset to ZERO and every message recorded four seconds of digital silence that sent, arrived and played as nothing — the recording overlay counted up happily throughout, because it animates on the CLOCK, not on audio. A meter fed from the encoder's input frames would have shown a flat bar the moment the kid spoke. Wants: the level computed where the PCM already is (the audio thread, before Opus), carried to the UI as a small int on the existing event/mailbox path rather than a new channel, and drawn with the view algebra's rects so it costs nothing on the 160x128 panel and works on the mac backend unchanged. Same bar on both clients
